newsitem.title: USA: Dow posts second biggest drop in history.
newsitem.headline: Dow posts second biggest drop in history.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average posted its second-biggest loss ever on Friday after an earnings warning by consumer products giant Gillette Co. and another drop in the dollar sent investors to the exit door.
Based on early and unofficial data, the blue-chip Dow closed down 247.37 points, or 3.11 percent, at 7,694.66, putting the index at its lowest close since June.
The drop was the steepest point fall since a plunge of 508 points on Oct. 19, 1987.
In the broader market, declining issues swamped advances 3-1 on active volume of 538 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Adding to the day's volatility was the "double-witching" expiration of options on stocks and stock indexes.
With the loss, the Dow has fallen 6.8 percent from its all-time closing high of 8,259.31, set on Aug. 6.
Several analysts said the downturn, the first sustained market decline since the nearly 10 percent correction that ended in mid-April, did not yet appear to be at its end.
"We are in a correction from the 8,300 level and we need to be tested a little further on the downside," said James Volk, head of institutional equity trading at Arcadia Investment Corp.

Wall Street was rattled by a warning from Gillette that it had guided analysts to pare back their earnings estimates for this year bacause of weak results at its Braun unit. Gillette slid 4-1/16 to 86.
The selling pressure dragged several consumer products companies lower, including Procter & Gamble Co., which skidded 7-3/4 to 136-11/16, the steepest decline among Dow components.
In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond hovered at Thursday's close of 6.55 percent.
